title: Libraries
intro: We enrich the lives of our military community by fostering opportunities for connection and providing equitable access to knowledge, innovation, and creativity.

sections.heading: Eligibility & Getting Started
sections.markdown:
#### Access Requirements

We welcome all eligible members of our military community.

The Library services extend to individuals across various sections of the military community. This includes:

• Active-Duty Service Members
• Dependent Children
• Dependent Spouses
• DoD Civilians
• DoD Families
• Host Nation Staff Members
• Medal of Honor Recipients
• National Guard
• Reservists
• Retirees
• 100% Disabled Veterans

These are generalized categories; eligibility per [DoDI 1015.10](https://www.esd.whs.mil/Portals/54/Documents/DD/issuances/dodi/101510p.pdf). Additional eligibility categories are determined per the installation commander. These additional categories do not extend access to the DoD MWR Virtual Library.

#### New to the Library?

Get started and explore your library today!

1. **Visit and Explore the Library** - Discover all the resources the library has to offer through our selection of books, digital media, innovative makerspaces, computers for adults and children, interactive programs, and more!
2. **Bring Identification** - Make sure you can provide the proper identification that verifies your eligibility for access to the library, such as a military ID card or dependent ID card.
3. **Library Account** - Create an account in-person at your local library, or start using virtual library resources now at [dodmwrlibraries.org](https://dodmwrlibraries.org/). Already have an account? Search, reserve, and manage your account at [milrec.bibliovation.com](https://milrec.bibliovation.com/).
4. **Ask Questions** - Don't hesitate to ask library staff if you have any questions about your account or available resources.

#### Guidelines and Rules

Help us maintain a space for shared learning and enjoyment.

• We want to provide a safe recreation and learning environment for our Marines and families.
• Library accounts are free for authorized users and can be obtained at the library using your official DoD ID card.
• Your Library account or DoD ID is required to check out materials and use the library's services.
• Most materials can be checked out for three weeks. Overdue notices will be sent first to the user's e-mail. Materials that are long overdue will result in your account being blocked and services suspended until the item is returned.
• Renew borrowed items online through our website or by contacting the library. There is a limit of two renewal times.
• Children are always welcome at the library. Children under ten years of age may not be left unattended. Libraries follow installation Child and Youth Supervision Guidelines and do not act in loco parentis.
• Tobacco products are not allowed within the library.

Library Policies
• [Marine Corps Order: 1700.33](https://www.marines.mil/News/Publications/MCPEL/Electronic-Library-Display/Article/900492/mco-170033/)
• Department of Defense Instruction: 1015.10

#### Borrowing Policy

Enjoy books, DVDs, video games and more!

• All materials borrowed from Marine Corps MWR General Libraries are for 3-week check outs.
• Unlimited Books
• DVDs Limit: 10 per family
• Audio Books Limit: 10 per family
• Playaways Limit: 2 per family
• Video Games Limit: 2 per family
• Library of Things/Boardgames/Equipment: Check with your local library for availability.
• Items may be renewed twice as long as an item has not been requested by another user. Please contact the library to renew or log into your account at milrec.bibliovation.com
• Sponsor is responsible for lost or damaged materials. Material replacements must be approved by the Library Director prior to purchase.

#### DoD MWR Virtual Library

Access resources and services through a centralized digital hub.

With its convenient access, the DoD MWR Virtual Library empowers service members and their families to pursue their intellectual and recreational interests, no matter where they are stationed.

Visit dodmwrlibraries.org to learn more.

The online platform provides access to a vast collection of digital materials available for online browsing and borrowing.

• E-books
• Audiobooks
• Magazines
• Newspapers
• Research Databases

Users can explore curated reading lists, access educational resources, and participate in virtual programs and events tailored to diverse interests and age groups.

Access library accounts at milrec.bibliovation.com, which offers user-friendly tools for searching, reserving, and managing library materials, as well as personalized features for creating wish lists and receiving recommendations.

#### Volunteering

Support your military community as a volunteer at the library.

Through volunteering, individuals can make a positive impact on their community, gain valuable experience in library operations, connect with others, and support the well-being and enrichment of military families.

Not all locations currently offer volunteering opportunities. Contact the local library for more information.

Contact the [Volunteer Coordinator](https://lejeunenewriver.usmc-mccs.org/marine-family-support/volunteer-opportunities) to learn about Volunteer Opportunities at your installation.

sections.heading: Programs, Resources & Information
sections.markdown:
#### Reading

Learn and development with our selection of books and resources.

Your base library is a valuable resource for lifelong learning and professional development. We offer a variety of reading services designed to support your educational and personal goals. Whether you're preparing for advancement, seeking to expand your knowledge base, or simply looking for a good book, our library provides the tools and resources you need to succeed. Discover the power of reading and unlock your full potential.

Reading Resources:

• Access to Overdrive by Libby
• Audiobooks
• Children & Teen Programming
• Children's Titles (Board Books through chapter books)
• Commandant of the Marine Corps Reading List
• DoD Summer Reading Program
• eBooks
• Early Childhood Literacy Programming and Resources
• Fiction and Nonfiction
• Marine Corps Professional Reading Program
• New Titles
• Paperback Book Kits for Deploying/Training units
• Storytimes
• Test Prep
• Young Adult/Teen titles

#### Electronics & Equipment

Explore and use equipment for personal and professional growth.

Your base library is a hub for practical learning and technological innovation. We offer electronics and equipment services designed to empower you with the skills and knowledge needed for success in a rapidly evolving world. From computer workstations and 3D printers to digital design software and specialized equipment, we provide the resources to support your educational and creative pursuits. Discover how our electronics and equipment services can help you build expertise and explore new possibilities.

• 3D Printers
• Black/White and Color Printing/Copying/Scanning
• CAC enabled Computers
• Charging Station
• Chompshop
• Faxing
• Gaming Consoles
• Makedo Tools
• Makerspace/Innovation Lab Equipment & Programming
• Video Games
• Virtual Reality/Augmented Reality
• WiFi access

Not all resources and services listed are available at each library. Contact or visit the library for availability.

#### Games & Movies

Discover our collection of games and movies available online and at your base library.

Recognizing the importance of recreation and mental resilience, your base library offers a wide selection of games and movies designed to provide relaxation and stress relief. We understand the unique demands of military life, and we strive to offer engaging entertainment that promotes well-being and fosters a sense of community.

• Board Games
• Children's DVD movies & TV series
• DVD movies & TV series
• Gaming Consoles (in-house use only)
• Video Games (Xbox/PlayStation/Switch)

Not available at all locations. Contact your local base library for availability.

For online resources visit our Virtual Library.

#### Additional Resources

Special features at the library that promote learning and development.

Beyond our core services, your base library offers a range of services designed to foster continuous learning and personal development. We provide access to resources and tools that empower you to explore new interests, enhance your skills, and expand your knowledge. Discover how our library can support your journey of lifelong learning.

• 24/7 Return Box
• Adult Programs
• Individual and Group Study Areas
• Library of Things (items may vary by location)
• Local Collections
• [Summer Reading Program](https://lejeunenewriver.usmc-mccs.org/marine-family-support/libraries/summer-reading-program)

Not all resources and services listed are available at each library.

Contact your local library for availability.

sections.heading: Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)
sections.markdown:
Find answers to commonly asked questions.

**Q: How do I register for library account?**
A: Visit the library with valid identification, typically a military ID or dependent ID, to register. For instant access to our online resources, please visit dodmwrlibraries.org.

**Q: What resources are available for children?**
A: Resources may include Storytime, educational computers, and age-appropriate programming, reading materials, DVDs, TV series, and launchpads for children. Each summer we also offer the DoD Summer Reading Program which is open to all ages. Contact your local installation library for more information.

**Q: Can I access the library's digital resources off-base?**
A: Yes, you can access our digital resources off-base by logging in to dodmwrlibraries.org. Access is authenticated through AAFEES.

**Q: How many items can I borrow at once?**
A: Patrons may borrow an unlimited number of books, 10 DVDs, and two video games at a time. Borrowing from the Library of Things collections vary by item type.

**Q: Are study rooms available?**
A: Study rooms are available at most installation libraries. Please contact us for more information and reservation details.

**Q: Can I access Wi-Fi at the library?**
A: Free Wi-Fi is available in the library.

**Q: Do you provide printing, copying, and scanning services?**
A: Yes, printing, copying, scanning, and faxing services are available for library patrons. Some locations charge a small fee for this service.

**Q: Are there programs and events for adults?**
A: Yes, we offer a variety of programs and events for adults. Check our calendar or contact us for details.

**Q: Can I renew borrowed items online?**
A: Yes, you can renew borrowed items online by logging into your account at milrec.bibliovation.com or by contacting the library. There is a limit of two renewals per item.

**Q: How do I access online databases?**
A: You can access databases and all our online resources by logging in to dodmwrlibraries.org and selecting Databases.

**Q: Do you provide assistance with research or academic projects?**
A: Our staff are available for reference assistance and can help connect you with our resources. Contact us for help or use the Contact Us form at dodmwrlibraries.org/contact-us.

**Q: Do you have collections dedicated to military-related topics?**
A: Yes, the Marine Corps MWR Library Program actively collects military history titles and supports the PME Marine Corps Professional Reading Program. You can find current titles by searching our catalog at milrec.bibliovation.com. If there is a specific title you are looking for, or need assistance with military-related items, please contact the library or use the Contact Us form at dodmwrlibraries.org/contact-us.

**Q: Can I donate books or materials to the library?**
A: In accordance with MCO 1700.33, the libraries do not accept donations of books or other materials. Please contact the library to see if there are any upcoming Book Swap/Art Swap/Puzzle Swap, etc. programs scheduled.

**Q: How do I access e-books and audiobooks?**
A: You can access e-books and audiobooks through our virtual library by logging in to dodmwrlibraries.org and selecting eBooks and Audiobooks.

**Q: What are the policies regarding overdue materials and penalties?**
A: Overdue materials may result in a blocked account for all account holders linked to a sponsor. Please return items promptly to avoid penalties. Contact the library if you need more time with an item.

**Q: What happens if I lose/damage library materials?**
A: Lost/damaged materials must be replaced and approved by the Library Director. Please contact the library prior to replacing an item to ensure that it will be accepted.
